Why contractors look for Angi alternatives

The complaints are consistent across trades. You pay for access to a homeowner whether or not you win the job. The same request can go to several pros, so speed matters more than quality. And when you stop paying, the leads stop, because you've been renting someone else's customers instead of building your own.

None of that makes marketplaces useless. They can be a reasonable way to fill gaps while you build something you own. The question is what that "something" should be.

How the big marketplaces charge

PlatformHow you payWatch out for
AngiPer lead, plus program fees depending on your planLeads may also go to other pros; read your contract terms
ThumbtackPer lead when you contact a customer or get auto-matched, no subscriptionYou pay even if the lead doesn't hire you; set a weekly budget
Google Local Services AdsPer lead (call or message), only in eligible trades and areasRequires screening; dispute invalid leads promptly
Yelp AdsPer click, with a budget you setStrong in some cities and trades, weak in others

Prices change often and vary by trade and zip code, so check the current numbers in your own area before comparing.

The alternative: leads that come to you

Every lead a marketplace sells you started as a homeowner searching Google. The long-term alternative is to show up in that search yourself, so the call comes straight to you and nobody else gets the same lead. That takes three pieces, and none of them is expensive.

1. A complete Google Business Profile

This is the listing in the map results. It's free, and once it has steady reviews it often brings in more calls than paid channels do. Pick the right primary category, list your service towns, and add real photos of your work.

2. Reviews you ask for every single time

Marketplaces show reviews on their platform, which you lose when you leave. Google reviews stay with you. Text a review link to every happy customer the day the job finishes. Here's how to get more Google reviews, with a message you can copy.

3. A page that turns searches into calls

When someone finds you, they want to know three things fast: do you do this job, do you cover my town, and how do I reach you. A simple page with your services, towns, a tap-to-call button and a quote form answers all three. Quote requests come straight to you. You don't pay per lead, and you don't compete with four other pros for the same homeowner.

That's what an Enoma page does. It's built from your Google listing, sends calls and quote requests straight to you, and costs $19.99/mo after a free first month: less than many single marketplace leads. See your page in 30 seconds.

A sensible way to switch

Don't cancel everything on day one. Most contractors who move away from shared leads do it in stages:

  1. Set up your Business Profile, review requests and your own page now.
  2. Track where every job comes from for a month or two. Ask "how did you find us?" on every call.
  3. Lower your marketplace budget as your own calls grow, and drop the platforms that cost the most per booked job.

The goal isn't zero paid leads. It's not depending on them.

Common questions

Angi alternatives for contractors who are done sharing leads: common questions

Is Angi worth it for contractors?

It can be for filling gaps, especially for new businesses. But you pay per lead whether or not you win the job, and leads can go to multiple pros. Many contractors use it short-term while building their own Google presence, then cut back as their own calls grow.

What is the best alternative to Angi and Thumbtack?

For most local contractors, the best long-term alternative is getting your own calls from Google: a complete Google Business Profile, steady reviews, and a simple website with your services, towns and a quote form. Those leads come only to you and don't cost per lead.

Do Thumbtack leads cost money even if I don't get the job?

Yes. Thumbtack charges when you contact a customer or are auto-matched to a lead, whether or not they hire you. You can set a weekly budget to cap spending.

How do I get leads without paying per lead?

Show up where homeowners search. Finish your Google Business Profile, ask every happy customer for a Google review, and have a page that names your services and towns with tap-to-call and a quote form. Referral asks and truck signage pointing to that page help too.
